sales.title:
JUDAEAN. First Jewish War.
Silver Shekel, dated year 2 = April 67 CE - March 68 CE. Temple (Jerusalem) mint.
Obv: Omer cup with beaded rim, date above; "Shekel of Israel" in Paleo-Hebrewscript around. Rev: sprig of three pomegranates; "Jerusalem the Holy" in Paleo-Hebrewscript around.

In secure plastic holder, graded NGC Ch XF Strike: 5/5 Surface: 4/5, certification number 8774685-001.

Struck at the Temple mint in Jerusalem during the second year of the First Jewish Revolt against Roman rule (April AD 67 - March AD 68), this silver shekel was issued at a pivotal stage of the conflict, when Jewish forces still retained control of Jerusalem and the Temple. Initially achieving considerable success, culminating in the defeat of the Roman governor Cestius Gallus at the Battle of Beth Horon. The scale of the uprising prompted Emperor Nero to appoint Vespasian to lead a major military campaign to retake Judaea. Although the rebellion was ultimately crushed with the destruction of Jerusalem and the Second Temple in 70, the shekels struck during its five dated years remain among the most historically important coinages of the ancient world, documenting the only silver coinage issued by an independent Jewish state until the modern era.

The obverse depicts an omer cup, generally interpreted as a sacred Temple vessel or the biblical measure used in religious offerings, while the reverse shows a sprig of three pomegranates, a traditional symbol of the priesthood and the decoration of the High Priest's garments. Struck in exceptionally pure silver, these shekels are widely believed to have served as the standard for payment of the annual Temple tax as well as circulating currency.

Certified by NGC as Choice Extremely Fine, with Strike 5/5 and Surface 4/5, this is an exceptional example of one of antiquity's most historically significant silver issues.

Reference: Deutsch-108; Hendin GBC 6, 6387; Hendin GBC 5, 1358; TJC-193; Sofaer 5-8.
Weight: 12.92g.
Diameter: 22mm.
Die Axis: 12h.
